angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 409,072 km at 136.89 pc = 0.04 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.3053 +/- 0.0233 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 136.89 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.588 +/- 0.011 solar radii from Hartman et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-5344 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..163H/abstract): 409,072 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.612 +/- 0.034 solar masses from Hartman et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-5344 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..163H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3747 +/- 64 K from Hartman et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5344 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..163H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hartman et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-5344 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166..163H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-5344.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.686, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
